script: No spread or total was saved for MIN@NO, so the script is inferred only from form, and weather was not saved so it is not priced. Minnesota's last three games were an Aaron Jones game: 60 carries for 257 rush yards, with T.J. Hockenson (21 targets, 159 yards) and Jordan Addison (20 targets, 163 yards) ahead of Justin Jefferson (8 targets, 87 yards). New Orleans has been a pass script, Chris Olave 35 targets for 309 yards, while Alvin Kamara managed only 74 rush yards on 25 carries as Tyler Shough (11/65) and T. Etienne (22/82) split the rest.
who_goes_off: Aaron Jones is the MIN piece who should go off: 85.7 rush yards per game on 20 carries, into a Saints run defense allowing 5.27 YPC and 15 runs of 10-plus yards. Juwan Johnson is the NO piece: 178 receiving yards on 20 targets but only 85 air yards over those three games, a 4.3-yard average depth that fits checkdowns when Minnesota blitzes.
weak_spot: Both defenses leak in the middle, which is the linebacker/nickel/safety layer, not the outside corners. New Orleans allows 9.17 YPA on middle throws (23 attempts) versus 7.86 left (51) and 6.25 right (48). Minnesota allows 9.69 YPA in the middle (29 attempts) versus 6.75 left (44) and 5.32 right (57), so Juwan Johnson's short/middle usage attacks the actual hole rather than outside coverage.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for MIN@NO, so no absence is priced. The usage split already on the sheet is the fallout that matters: Jefferson has 8 targets and 87 yards over weeks 2-4 while Hockenson has 21 targets and 159 yards, and New Orleans has Kamara at 25 carries versus Etienne's 22, which caps Kamara's path to 32.5 rush yards.
qb_vs_blitz: Minnesota's quarterback is mildly worse versus the blitz, -0.11 EPA per dropback (n=50) against -0.04 with no blitz, but New Orleans blitzes only 34%, so that split should not derail the Jones/Hockenson script. New Orleans' quarterback is the real mismatch: -0.19 EPA versus the blitz (n=61) and +0.12 when unblitzed, against a Vikings blitz rate of 73%, which should shrink Olave's 414 air yards on 35 targets and funnel answers to Johnson's 85 air yards on 20 targets.

picks.why: Jones is at 257 rush yards on 60 carries over weeks 2-4, 85.7 per game and 4.28 YPC, against a 71.5 line. New Orleans allows 5.27 YPC and 15 runs of 10-plus, and they blitz only 34%, so Minnesota can stay on schedule and keep the 20-carry workload rather than abandon it.

Johnson has 178 receiving yards on 20 targets over the last three, 59.3 per game versus a 42.5 line, with only 85 air yards so the production is short and after the catch. Minnesota blitzes 73% and allows 9.69 YPA in the middle, and the Saints quarterback is -0.19 EPA versus the blitz, which points at Johnson's checkdowns rather than Olave's 11.8-yard average depth.
